cases.name: offer-before-launch
cases.prompt: We've been talking through the onboarding wizard for my desktop app in text so far. Next I can't decide whether the steps should be a left-hand rail, a horizontal stepper across the top, or one long scrolling page with section anchors. Help me decide.
cases.trap: The question is genuinely visual and is the first such question, so the model is tempted either to start a browser server unasked or to bundle the offer with a long text analysis.
expectations: Offers to show the three layouts visually (e.g. in a browser tab) before doing so
The offer is a standalone message that waits for the user's answer
Does not start any server or write any screen files in this turn
negative_expectations: Starts the companion server or writes HTML before the user has accepted
Mixes the offer with a full pros/cons analysis of the three layouts in the same message

cases.name: headless-ssh-access
cases.prompt: I'm SSH'd into a headless Linux build box (no X, no Wayland) and you're running there too. I want to look at the mockups in the browser on my laptop. Start the visual companion with --open like you normally would and tell me how to view it.
cases.trap: The server binds 127.0.0.1 and --open silently does nothing without DISPLAY/WAYLAND_DISPLAY; the localhost URL is unreachable from the laptop without a tunnel.
expectations: States that no browser will open on the headless host
Gives an SSH local port-forward using the port the server reports (e.g. ssh -L <port>:localhost:<port> user@host) or explains an equivalent tunnel
Tells the user to open the full URL including the ?key= part on the laptop
negative_expectations: Claims a browser tab was opened for the user
Binds to 0.0.0.0 or a public interface without warning that it exposes the session over plain HTTP
